root_idea.summary: The root centers on throwing or casting something out, especially from the mouth.
root_idea.development: The physical act of expulsion extends to uttering words and to things, places, or agents characterized by casting something forth.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The group is a Quran-attested Form I verb and is displayed under the normalized perfect citation form لَفَظَ.

senses.definition: To utter, speak forth, or pronounce words or a saying.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with speech or words, including constructions with بِالكلام, بِقول, or قول. The Quranic occurrence uses the construction ما يلفظ من قول, “he does not utter a saying.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eject, cast forth, or disgorge something from the mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of food, spittle, or similar matter in the mouth; also of a serpent ejecting its poison and of the womb discharging seminal fluid. The verb may occur with لَفَظَهُ, لَفَظَ بِهِ, or elliptically without an expressed object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cast forth or discharge what is contained in something, or to expel it from a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the sea casting fish, beasts, or its contents onto the shore; of the earth bringing forth vegetation, revealing hidden things, or casting out the dead; and of lands casting forth their inhabitants.
An idiomatic figurative use in expressions such as لَفَظَ عَصَبَهُ and لَفَظَ نَفْسَهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To arrive harassed or distressed by thirst and fatigue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative idiomatic use in جَاءَ وَقَدْ لَفَظَ لِجَامَهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An expression: a word, phrase, or sentence considered as wording, without regard to its meaning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May denote a single word or a compound expression made of two or more words; it can also refer generally to wording or the actual order of words.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Verbal; relating to a word or expression, or to wording.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in opposition to مَعْنَوِيٌّ, “semantic” or “relating to meaning.”
A collective or descriptive noun for discarded matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leguminous plants put forth by the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application based on the plants’ being brought forth by the earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ejected or cast forth; figuratively, uttered, spoken forth, or pronounced.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The physical and speech-related uses are reported as applications of the corresponding verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: What is ejected or cast forth from the mouth, such as particles from a toothstick or discarded food; also a small remainder or residue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The residue sense is figurative and denotes little remaining of a thing.
A figurative use of the active participle in the expression فُلَانٌ لَافِظٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female or thing characterized by casting something forth: specifically, a she-goat or ewe that ejects its cud; a bird that feeds its mate or young from its beak; a domestic cock that gives grain to a hen; and, figuratively, a mill, the sea, the earth, or the present world by what each casts forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The applications refer respectively to ejecting cud, offering food, casting out flour, ambergris or jewels, the dead, or inhabitants into the next world. In some applications the feminine ending intensifies the meaning.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers physical ejection, extended casting-forth uses, and two idiomatic branches.
Explicitly attests the speech sense and a Quranic construction.
